caption:

A bunion is a change in the angle of the big toe joint, and genetics and foot shape play a big part. Exercises and shoes usually won't straighten the toe, but they can ease pain, reduce pressure on the bump and keep you walking comfortably.

Start with a wide, deep toe box and a few minutes of toe spreading and big-toe lifts most days.

A red, hot or quickly swelling joint, numb toes or a sore over the bump are worth checking promptly, especially if you have diabetes. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.

A sneeze is a fast, forceful squeeze of your trunk muscles, often while you're slightly bent or twisted. If your back is already tired from long sitting, poor sleep or a busy week, that sudden load can set off a spasm.

Early on, gentle movement, short walks and heat often help, and most acute back pain settles over days to a few weeks. Next time, stand tall with soft knees and a hand on a wall.

Desk all week, golf all weekend, and Toto's swing just isn't turning like it used to.

Golf, tennis, cricket and paddling all rely on rotation, and the mid-back between your shoulder blades is built to provide a good chunk of it. After long desk days it often stiffens, and the lower back and shoulders pick up the slack.

Try the quick check: sit, cross your arms and turn each way. Then open books and thread-the-needle, eight slow reps most days. An adjustment can help it feel looser short term, and the change tends to hold better with regular movement and strength work.

caption:
Ever lain there thinking "that's way too much" and said nothing? Momo has.

Harder isn't automatically better. Many people get more out of firm but comfortable pressure that lets muscles relax rather than brace. A simple 0 to 10 scale helps: around 5 to 7 is often a good zone, and if you're holding your breath, it's too much.

You can ask for more, less or a different area at any time. Mention recent injuries, easy bruising or pregnancy. Massage works well alongside active rehab rather than replacing it.

After a sprain, the ankle can lose some strength and some of its sense of where it is. If rehab stops as soon as the pain fades, it may not react as quickly on an uneven path or an awkward landing.

The good news: balance and strength are trainable. Start with 30 seconds on one leg while brushing your teeth, add single-leg calf raises and band work, then build to small hops and side-to-side drills over several weeks. Handy before summer beach runs.

caption:
Shoulders and neck feeling it after the first few surfs of summer? 🏄

Most of surfing is paddling. That's hundreds of strokes per session with your neck extended to look ahead, which is a big jump after a quiet winter.

A few things tend to help. Build session length up over a few weeks rather than going straight to three-hour mornings. Add band external rotations, rows and face-down Y raises on land two or three times a week. And give your neck a short rest between sets.

Pain that wakes you at night, weakness lifting your arm or pins and needles down the arm are worth getting assessed. Our Sydney CBD and Chatswood physios can build a plan around your surf days. Book online via the link in bio.
